title: Weekly POC sync - signal triage & guardrail tune with Ivybridge Diagnostics
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on recent regression in entity extraction recall, investigation of false-positive guardrail triggers, prompt-set pruning proposal, and an action plan for targeted evals and a short benchmarking job on Redwood Dedicated. Next steps: Redwood to run 24-hour sampling run, share guardrail rule debug logs, customer to provide 150 failing prompt examples, schedule a focused deep-dive next Wed.

Quality scoring thresholds and scorecard drift
Mini-benchmark on Dedicated vs Hosted for latency variability

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Cassidy (Redwood AE), Mateo (Redwood SE), Anya (Redwood CSM), Priya (Ivybridge Head of Data), Liam (Ivybridge ML Eng), Sana (Ivybridge PM), Evan (Ivybridge Security)

Summary / Auto notes (auto-generated, may be partial):
- Quick health check on scorecard trends, regression spike in entity extraction recall the last 48h
- Guardrail false positive increase after new prompt set ingestion
- Agreed to run targeted sampling + short dedicated benchmark
- Action items captured at end

Transcript:
[00:00] Cassidy (Redwood): All right folks, thanks for joining. We'll run through the quality pulse, the regression you called out, and then walk through guardrail noise. Mateo and I will share some logs and a plan. Priya, do you want to open with the impact?
[00:18] Priya (Ivybridge): Yeah thanks. So over the past two days we saw recall on patient-identifier extraction drop from 95 to about 86 on the critical subset. It's mostly short IDs in clinical notes, those with hyphens and nested parentheses. It's causing downstream match failures and the triage UI to mis-route.
[00:35] Liam (Ivybridge): I also want to note some of the false positives — the guardrail has been flagging benign institution names as PHI and blocking workflows. We think this started after we ingested the expanded prompt set last week.
[00:52] Mateo (Redwood): Got it. Quick question: when you say "expanded prompt set" was it the user-facing templates or the internal canonicalization changes? Sometimes small changes to the preamble shift decoding behavior.
[01:05] Sana (Ivybridge): It was both, sorry. We rolled a handful of short templates for the front-end and also normalized a couple canonical prompts to fix tone. My bad if that caused drift.
[01:16] Cassidy (Redwood): No worries, that's what these syncs are for. We'll take a look at the exact prompts. Mateo, quick status on the scorecard — what's the delta and any sign it's model-side vs prompt-side?
[01:29] Mateo (Redwood): From the initial logs the drop looks correlated with a cluster of low-confidence token probs on the entity spans — so likely model-side sensitivity amplified by new prefixes. I want to be careful: could be KV cache behavior or even a latency-induced truncation, we saw a couple requests timeout at the tail. There's also a chance it interacts with the guardrail post-processing.
[01:50] Evan (Ivybridge): On timeouts — we haven't changed client timeouts, but we did see increased p90 latency yesterday which correlates with the recall drop.
[02:03] Cassidy (Redwood): Ok — action item for Mateo to run a sampling job and pull the low-confidence set. We'll do a 24-hour sampling across your traffic slice to avoid selection bias.
[02:15] Priya (Ivybridge): That'd be great. Also, for the guardrail false positives, we need a way to triage rules — currently it's a binary block which is too heavy. Any ideas short-term?
[02:28] Mateo (Redwood): We can add an alert-only mode for suspect rules so they don't block, just surface in the UI. But that requires the front-end change on your side or we can add a shadow flag. For the immediate term, we can lower severity for the institution-name rule and add a whitelist override.
[02:45] Liam (Ivybridge): Whitelist's good but we need full reproducible examples. We'll upload failing prompts — I'll put at least 150 examples with raw input and expected extraction.
[02:58] Cassidy (Redwood): Perfect. If you can do that by Friday we can run canonical re-eval on Monday.
[03:06] Priya (Ivybridge): Aim for Friday EOD.
[03:10] (brief crosstalk)
[03:20] Mateo (Redwood): I'm noticing in the logs some mis-tagging where the model labels institution names as 'patient' when the prompt contains words like 'admission to' — likely a short-context disambiguation error. Could be sequence length influence. Are you truncating long notes client-side?
[03:34] Liam (Ivybridge): We do truncate to 1024 tokens in the pipeline. Mostly we keep the section around the extraction target but we do compress long historic notes.
[03:44] Mateo (Redwood): That could be it — if the nearby context that disambiguates isn't present, recall drops. Two mitigations: 1) tweak the client to include a small window of left context for entity targets; 2) run a small Dedicated-based benchmark to check if higher memory models or different quantization changes behavior.
[04:05] Priya (Ivybridge): How long would a Dedicated benchmark take and what's the cost?
[04:11] Cassidy (Redwood): We can spin a 2-GPU short job (2 hours) to replay a representative batch and capture latency percentiles + token costs. It's relatively low cost for a pilot — we'll share exact numbers in the notes. Mateo will set it up.
[04:25] Sana (Ivybridge): Is there a chance this is from the guardrail post-processor? We've got the normalization step that conflates some institution suffixes with patient fields.
[04:34] Mateo (Redwood): Possible; sometimes post-processing rules use regexes that are too greedy. Send us an example of the rule and we'll run it against the failing set.
[04:44] Priya (Ivybridge): We'll include the rule snippets in the upload.
[04:49] (pause)
[05:05] Cassidy (Redwood): Ok let's jump to scoring. On your scorecard, which thresholds moved and did you adjust any weights?
[05:14] Sana (Ivybridge): We bumped the precision threshold for high-priority entities from 0.9 to 0.92 after a business decision, but the recall drop is now causing us to fail the gate — so we need to tune scoring or the prompts.
[05:27] Mateo (Redwood): We recommend a two-pronged approach: prompt canonicalization (so the input distribution matches training) and temporary threshold relaxation for the affected entity while we debug. Also consider running a small reranking pass focused on entity likelihoods.
[05:42] Liam (Ivybridge): Reranking might add latency. Our UI is sensitive — any added step needs to be low-latency (<200ms extra ideally).
[05:52] Mateo (Redwood): Understood. The rerank can be async for non-blocking flows; for blocking flows, we can do a lightweight confidence calibration which is cheaper.
[06:02] Priya (Ivybridge): On calibration — do you provide token-level probs in the hosted API?
[06:08] Cassidy (Redwood): Yes, we can surface token-level confidences and an overall span confidence. Mateo will include the sampling output with token probs. Keep in mind sometimes the wordpiece alignment in outputs is noisy in the transcription, we call it out in the logs.
[06:24] (short chuckle)
[06:30] Mateo (Redwood): Minor note — the logs show some requests returning slightly different entity boundaries across near-duplicate prompts. That's often due to sampling temperature or decoding change. Can you confirm your client isn't setting temperature?
[06:42] Liam (Ivybridge): No, temperature is default 0.0 in our pipeline. But we did change the max tokens param in a recent deploy.
[06:51] Mateo (Redwood): Could be related. We'll enumerate recent config diffs in the debug log.
[06:58] Cassidy (Redwood): All right, next section: guardrail noise. Priya, you mentioned the institution false positives — any pattern on which institutions are flagged?
[07:07] Priya (Ivybridge): Mostly shorter names with numeric suffixes, like 'North-2 Lab' — the hyphen and numeral seems to trip the rule.
[07:16] Mate o (Redwood): (mis-transcribed) — "Mate o" meaning Mateo — Sorry, saw a typo in my client. For hyphen numeral cases, we can add a rule that checks token context and applies heuristics. But that's brittle at scale. Longer-term we should add a learned filter step that classifies candidate spans as entity vs organization.
[07:33] Evan (Ivybridge): Security question: if we add a learned filter, where does training data live? We need to ensure it's within our Private deployment for compliance.
[07:42] Cassidy (Redwood): Good call. For anything that touches PHI-sensitive data, we recommend Private or Dedicated with customer-managed keys. Redwood can run the filter in your VPC if you go private. For the POC, the short-term approach is rule whitelists and shadow mode.
[07:56] Priya (Ivybridge): Shadow mode would help diagnose without impacting production.
[08:01] (transition)
[08:12] Mateo (Redwood): On metrics, we noticed an uptick in guardrail-triggered events around 03/03 22:00 UTC — I'm pulling an event diff now. The interesting bit is many of those were high-confidence from the model but the post-filter marked them. That suggests post-filter over-aggressive regexes.
[08:33] Liam (Ivybridge): We'll attach the regexes in the upload. Also, can Redwood annotate the examples with the model's token-level probs? That would help us decide whether to change the rule or the model.
[08:45] Cassidy (Redwood): Yes — Mateo will attach token probs in the sampling CSV.
[08:50] Sana (Ivybridge): Quick product ask: is there a way in the Console to see a diff of scorecard metrics pre/post prompt change?
[08:58] Anya (Redwood CSM): We have a delta view but it's on a two-week window by default. We can pull a custom window for you and pin the change points. I'll prepare a snapshot.
[09:08] Priya (Ivybridge): That snapshot would be helpful to show execs.
[09:12] (short pause)
[09:22] Mateo (Redwood): Now, about prompt-set pruning — small tip: canonicalize critical entities using explicit tokens in the prompt rather than relying on free-form text. For example, include a 'target_entity: [----]' line to reduce ambiguity.
[09:37] Liam (Ivybridge): We'll try that. Can you share examples of canonicalization templates?
[09:42] Cassidy (Redwood): We'll add a short PR with three canonical templates and the before/after expected behaviors.
[09:49] Priya (Ivybridge): Another note, we had two different teams pushing similar templates which may have collided. We'll do a quick sweep to de-dupe.
[09:57] (crosstalk)
[10:10] Mateo (Redwood): Ok next, Dedicated vs Hosted — you asked for guidance last week on whether moving to Dedicated could reduce variance. For many models the Dedicated environment gives more stable p95 latency and deterministic quantization paths, so it's worth testing.
[10:25] Sana (Ivybridge): How deterministic are we talking? Our clients need consistent response times for interactive workflows.
[10:32] Mateo (Redwood): In our experience p95 improved by 20-35% on Dedicated in similar workloads, and token generation determinism is better when you pin runtime kernels. But results depend on model, batching, and peak concurrency. The short benchmark will quantify that for your workload.
[10:49] Priya (Ivybridge): That helps. Could the Dedicated benchmark also show unit-cost delta so we can weigh economics?
[10:55] Cassidy (Redwood): Yes we'll include token cost and an estimated monthly extrapolation.
[11:02] (pause)
[11:15] Liam (Ivybridge): Regarding the low-confidence set — what format do you want for the examples? JSONL with fields input, expected_entities, context?
[11:23] Mateo (Redwood): JSONL is perfect. Include raw_input, expected_spans with start/end and label, any pre/post processing steps. If you can add a short flag 'blocking_flow: true' for those that must not be missed, that's helpful.
[11:36] Liam (Ivybridge): Will do.
[11:39] Cassidy (Redwood): Ok let's capture the concrete owners again. Cassidy will own the logistics and pricing snapshot; Mateo does the sampling and Dedicated spin; Liam and Priya provide failing examples and rule snippets; Sana will update scorecard success criteria.
[11:55] Priya (Ivybridge): One process question: when we get the sampling CSV, will it include raw text or redacted? We can't share PHI in the POC unless it's redacted.
[12:05] Cassidy (Redwood): We recommend you redact before upload. Redwood can also accept hashed identifiers if needed. For the Dedicated benchmark inside a customer VPC, we can run with unredacted data if you move to Private later and sign the SOW. For now redacted examples are fine.
[12:23] Evan (Ivybridge): From a security standpoint, we'll redact but include annotation metadata so the model context remains representative.
[12:32] (transition)
[12:45] Mateo (Redwood): For the run plan: I'll kick off a 24-hour sampling starting tonight, collecting low-confidence spans and token probs. Then next week we can do a 2-hour Dedicated replay using a 10k-sample slice. Should have numbers within 48 hours.
[13:03] Sana (Ivybridge): Sounds good. Quick question on guardrail throttling — can you throttle alert volume so our SRE isn't flooded?
[13:11] Cassidy (Redwood): Yes we have alert aggregation and rate-limiting; Anya will configure a conservative rate so you get a digest instead of per-event pings.
[13:21] Anya (Redwood CSM): I'll set that up and share the alert digest schedule.
[13:28] (brief)
[13:40] Priya (Ivybridge): Any recommended temporary prompt tweaks to reduce false positives while we debug?
[13:46] Mateo (Redwood): Insert explicit negative examples in the prompt: show the model examples of institution names that are NOT PHI. That often reduces over-generalization. Also reduce the early prefix that may bias the model.
[13:59] Liam (Ivybridge): We'll test negative-example prompts.
[14:03] Cassidy (Redwood): Ok near the end here — recap of owners and deadlines. Cassidy: share pricing snapshot and guardrail debug link by 2026-03-07. Mateo: 24-hr sampling results and token prob CSV by 2026-03-08 and provision Dedicated benchmark. Liam: upload 150 failing examples by 2026-03-06. Sana: update scorecard and confirm go/no-go thresholds by 2026-03-09.
[14:28] Priya (Ivybridge): Agree. Also schedule the Wed deep-dive.
[14:32] Cassidy (Redwood): Will send calendar invite for 2026-03-11 16:00 UTC.
[14:36] (closing chatter)
[14:50] Evan (Ivybridge): One last security note: we'll need an IP allowlist for any Dedicated endpoints if you spin those up.
[14:58] Cassidy (Redwood): Noted — we'll include the network requirements in the bench notes.
[15:05] (meeting winds down)
[15:20] Cassidy (Redwood): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the thread.
[15:25] (end)

Notes about transcription: Some speaker labels may be approximate; a couple of brand names were auto-transcribed (e.g., "KV cache" read as "K-V cake"). Links mentioned: guardrail debug link (internal Redwood ticket), dedicated bench request form (shared by Cassidy), scorecard snapshot (to be attached by Anya).
